name: Foot Sweeps (Kouchi, Sasae, De Ashi)
keyCorrections: If the foot won't move: you didn't off-balance first — pull them onto the foot, then sweep
If you keep getting guillotined: your head is dropping — keep your head up and spine tall
If the sweep doesn't disrupt their base: your timing is off — sweep as the foot lands, not before
description: A system of foot sweeps adapted from Judo for no-gi BJJ. These techniques use timing, off-balancing (kuzushi), and precise foot placement to take down an opponent with minimal effort. Key sweeps include Kouchi Gari (inner reap), Sasae Tsurikomi Ashi (supporting foot block), and De Ashi Harai (forward foot sweep). Popularized in no-gi by Gordon Ryan, Garry Tonon, and the Danaher Death Squad.
shortInstruction: Create off-balancing with collar ties and wrist control, sweep the foot as it receives weight, and chain into double legs when the opponent steps back.
summary: Foot sweeps exploit the opponent's weight transfer during stance fighting. When the opponent is focused on defending double legs, their weight shifts predictably, making them vulnerable. In no-gi, collar ties, wrist control, and two-on-one grips create the necessary off-balancing. The key sweeps are Kouchi Gari (inner reap with circular pull), Sasae (blocking the advancing foot), and De Ashi Harai (sweeping the foot as it touches the mat).
whyItWorks: Exploits predictable weight transfer when the opponent defends other takedowns
Requires minimal energy compared to high-commitment takedowns
Sets up higher commitment attacks by creating reactions
Constantly threatens even when you can't shoot for a double leg
commonMistakes: Sweeping without off-balancing first — the foot will be planted and cannot move
Dropping your head forward during the sweep, exposing the guillotine
Using only leg strength instead of coordinating upper body pull
Sweeping too early or too late — timing is everything
Not chaining — a foot sweep should lead into a double leg if partially blocked
coachingCues: The hands set up the sweep — create the reaction, then take it
Stay tall — head up, chest up throughout
Sweep the foot as it touches, not before
Chain sweeps: miss Kouchi → go Sasae → go double leg
safetySummary: Keep your head up to avoid guillotine counters when sweeping
Be aware of the opponent snapping you down as you close distance
Foot sweeps are low-risk — you stay on your feet and maintain distance

systemLogic.corePrinciple: Foot sweeps have 3 branches: Kouchi Gari → Sasae → De Ashi Harai

decisionTree.condition: Opponent steps back from Kouchi attempt

decisionTree.action: Sasae — block their advancing foot and pull them over it
De Ashi Harai — catch their circling foot and sweep laterally

moneyDetails: Foot sweeps are the lowest-energy takedowns in no-gi — use them to tire opponents
Garry Tonon and Gordon Ryan use foot sweeps to set up their entire standup game
Mastering foot sweeps eliminates the need to 'muscle' takedowns against larger opponents
fixItFast: If foot won't move: off-balance first — pull and then sweep
If guillotined: keep your head up, stay tall
If sweep fails: chain into a double leg immediately
